subject.title: feat(channels): core-owned durable ingress drain — one turn-adoption lifecycle for Telegram and WhatsApp

question: Should OpenClaw permanently expose `openChannelIngressDrain` and the turn-adoption lifecycle as a supported plugin SDK/runtime contract, with Telegram and WhatsApp migrated together in this PR?
rationale: The contributor’s recommended boundary is technically coherent, but it creates a lasting plugin API and compatibility commitment; the protected maintainer label and prior review discussion do not contain an actual maintainer-authored approval of that permanent surface.

options.title: Approve the narrowed core seam
options.body: Accept core ownership and the limited public drain/lifecycle API, subject to a clean rebase, surface checks, compatibility proof, and live WhatsApp evidence.

options.title: Keep the drain internal
options.body: Centralize the bundled Telegram and WhatsApp implementations in core but remove the new public plugin runtime and SDK exports until an external consumer proves the API requirement.

options.title: Split the migration
options.body: Land the core and Telegram ownership change separately and defer the WhatsApp adapter until its real linked-account behavior can be demonstrated.

recommendation.title: Approve the narrowed core seam
recommendation.body: Accept core ownership and the limited public drain/lifecycle API, subject to a clean rebase, surface checks, compatibility proof, and live WhatsApp evidence.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent merged work owns the SDK-surface narrowing and shared channel-runtime boundary most directly affected by this decision.
